costNote: The energy itself: fuel burned in Ameren's power plants and electricity bought from others, plus gas bought for resale — $837M total. Utilities pass much of this through to customers, so the real business is the margin on top.

opex.note: Running the grid and plants — this year heavier tree-trimming and energy-center maintenance nudged it up.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wearing out a very large asset base — and growing, as Ameren keeps investing in grid infrastructure.

otherDetail.note: Interest on the debt that finances the grid build-out.

footerNote: Utility layout: fuel, purchased power and gas bought for resale are shown as the direct-cost block; depreciation and property-type taxes sit in running costs. Net income is the consolidated $677M; $676M was attributable to common shareholders.

segments.name: Electric
segments.note: Electricity for Missouri and Illinois — 94% of revenue. Warmer weather lifted Missouri retail sales, and regulated investment in the grid earns a growing return.

segments.name: Natural gas
segments.note: Gas delivery — a small, seasonal slice that matters more in winter.

sources.label: Ameren Q3 2026 earnings release — SEC EDGAR Ex-99.1 (8-K, Nov 5, 2026)

takeaways.text: EPS of $2.42 matched the adjusted figure and rose versus adjusted $2.17 a year ago (GAAP $2.35 included a one-off tax benefit). Infrastructure investment and warm-weather sales did the work.
takeaways.title: Clean quarter, no adjustments

takeaways.text: Ameren raised 2026 guidance to $5.35–$5.55, set 2027 at $5.70–$5.90, and guided to 8–10% annual EPS growth for 2027–2031 — top-tier for a regulated utility.
takeaways.title: Growth guidance stands out

takeaways.text: Interest charges of $216M ate about a quarter of operating income — the flip side of funding a multi-year grid build with debt.
takeaways.title: Debt funds the build

verdict: The regulated-utility script, executed: grid investment plus warm weather delivered $2.42 a share and a guidance raise.
